newsitem.title: USA: Lilly sees Q4 EPS in line with estimates.
newsitem.headline: Lilly sees Q4 EPS in line with estimates.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said Friday that sales of its new anti-schizophrenia drug, Zyprexa, are strong, and the company expects fourth quarter financial results to be in line with Wall Street projections.
"We are very pleased with Zyprexa sales for the fourth quarter," said Lilly spokesman Jim Kappel. "We expect our financial results to fall in line with consensus estimates."

The Indianapolis-based drugmaker is expected to report fourth quarter profits in late January of $0.69 per share, up from year-ago profits of $0.57 per share, according to the First Call consensus of 20 drug industry analysts' estimates.
Alex. Brown analyst Barbara Ryan said Lilly could beat that figure "by a tiny bit."
Sales of Zyprexa are exploding, said Rodman & Renshaw analyst James Keeney, who estimated shipments of the recently approved drug are running at more than $1 million daily.
"We now believe that Zyprexa sales could reach as high as an astounding $80 million in the quarter," Keeney said.

"Despite Zyprexa sales exceeding all expectations, we are not raising our fourth quarter 1996 forecast of $0.69 (per share). We expect Lilly to take offsetting reserves in the quarter for as yet unknown reasons," Keeney said.
He added that the company has been expected for some time to take a charge against its PCS Health Systems Inc unit.
"For the quarter, there are no special charges related to PCS," Kappel said, adding he could not comment on analysts' speculations.
Shares in Lilly closed up 5/8 at 76-3/8 Friday.
